actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a control, motion-planning, bimanual-coordination and reinforcement-learning platform for the Enactic OpenArm v2 (7-DOF x 2 plus grippers) in MuJoCo
The package maps the scene name 'unscrew' to v2/openarm_mujoco_v2/unscrew_scene.xml
The unscrew scene is the MJCF model openarm_v20_unscrew with a 0.002 s integration timestep
The unscrew scene declares openarm_pedestal.xml as an attachable model asset and attaches model arm_pedestal in its worldbody
The pedestal model declares openarm_v20_bimanual.xml as an attachable model asset and attaches model bimanual at a frame 0.698 m above the pedestal origin
The bimanual model is the MJCF model openarm_v20_visual with 16 position actuators, eight per arm (seven joints and one finger)

The left arm control ranges are joint1 -3.49066 to 1.39626 rad, joint2 -3.31613 to 0.174533 rad, joint3 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad, joint4 0 to 2.44346 rad, joint5 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad, joint6 -0.785398 to 0.785398 rad, joint7 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad and the finger 0 to 0.7854

The right arm control ranges are joint1 -1.39626 to 3.49066 rad, joint2 -0.174533 to 3.31613 rad, joint3 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad, joint4 0 to 2.44346 rad, joint5 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad, joint6 -0.785398 to 0.785398 rad, joint7 -1.5708 to 1.5708 rad and the finger -0.7854 to 0
The scene adds the cap_lift_drive position actuator on the cap_lift joint with control range 0 to 0.12
The cap has a hinge turn joint and a slide lift joint with a 0 to 0.12 range
The ready keyframe states nq = 20 as left arm coordinates 0-8, right arm coordinates 9-17, cap_turn 18 and cap_lift 19
Each hand's two finger joints are coupled by a joint equality constraint
The arm joint classes motor_DM8009, motor_DM4340, motor_DM4310 and motor_DM3507 default to hinge joints, and the finger class defaults to a limited hinge joint
The package requires Python 3.10 or newer, pins mujoco==3.8.1 and depends on numpy
The unscrew demo loads the scene with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, creates MjData and resets to the ready keyframe
The implementation log describes the single-arm unscrew scene as a clamped bottle whose threaded cap has a turn hinge, a lift slide and a lift actuator
The OpenArm v2 MuJoCo model under v2/openarm_mujoco_v2 (meshes and MJCF) is attributed to Enactic, Inc. under Apache-2.0

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so the same ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene, follows the attachable models openarm_pedestal.xml and openarm_v20_bimanual.xml, and takes the 2 ms step, the 20 qpos coordinates, the 20 dof coordinates and the 17 actuator ctrlranges from that tree, then moves each actuated joint toward its control target; it computes no inertias, contacts, tendons, finger equalities or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result

the stand-in inserts an attached model's actuators at the attach element in document order (the 16 arm actuators, then the scene's cap_lift actuator); MuJoCo was not installed where the gate runs, so the engine's ctrl index order was not confirmed against this stand-in
the meshes and textures under v2/openarm_mujoco_v2/assets are not loaded by the stand-in; a real engine load needs them beside the scene, which the pinned clone provides

the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (zero qpos in the stand-in), not from the ready keyframe of unscrew_scene.xml:85-91; a client that wants that pose must send its qpos and step
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 2 ms step only
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the scene's tablecam and frontcam are not exposed as an observation, only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is
the upstream task logic on top of the model (UnscrewTask, the demo controller and its rewards) is not served; this package exposes the raw simulated model
the stand-in snapshot covers time, qpos, qvel and ctrl only; MuJoCo's mjSTATE_INTEGRATION also covers act, warm-start and mocap fields, which this model does not use
the model is a simulation asset for OpenArm: no physical arm is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
